newsitem.title: USA: Washington Nat'l holder opposes deal.
newsitem.headline: Washington Nat'l holder opposes deal.

text.p: Paulson & Co, an investment management firm with a 6.2 percent stake in Washington National Corp, said it opposes the life insurer's proposed merger with PennCorp Financial Group, calling the terms of the deal "inadequate."
PennCorp agreed in November to acquire Washington National for $29.50 a share in cash and stock in a deal valued at $400 million.
But John Paulson, a principal with Paulson & Co, said that the price negotiated nine months ago is no longer adequate in today's marketplace.
The price PennCorp agreed to pay was below book value. But other life insurers have been sold recently at much higher values, he said.

Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV agreed to buy Equitable of Iowa Cos for 2.6 times book value and Lincoln National Corp agreed to buy CIGNA Corp's individual life insurance business for three times book value, he said.

"This deal was announced almost nine months ago and over the course of the nine months the valuation multiples both public and private have risen considerably," Paulson said in a a telephone interview with Reuters.
"So the price they negotiated nine months ago does not appear adequate in today's market environment," he said.
PennCorp was not immediately available for comment. Washington National declined immediate comment.

In a letter to Washington National chief executive Robert Patin, Paulson said he would support a plan that would allow the deal to expire on August 30, if PennCorp were unwilling to raise its bid, and have Morgan Stanley, the company's investment banker, re-solicit potential purchasers.

In addition, given the increase in life insurance valuations since the deal was announced, he said he doubted Morgan Stanley would be able to update its fairness opinion on the deal at the $29.50 a share price.

PennCorp, a New York-based insurance holding company, underwrites and markets life, annuities and accident insurance through its subsidiaries to the middle market in the United States, Canada and Caribbean.
An investment fund affiliated with PennCorp earlier this week agreed to participate in a management buyout of the insurance brokerage operations of Acordia Inc from Anthem Inc.
Knightsbridge Capital LLC, the general partner of Knightsbridge Capital Fund, which is affiliated with PennCorp and Wand Partners, agreed to pay $320 million in cash and debt for Acordia.

Washington National, based in Lincolnshire, Ill., is an insurance holding company whose two main operating subsidiaries are Washington National Insurance Co, a writer of disability products to the educator market, and United Presidential Life, a writer of universal life products.
